answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
